note_claims.claim: The patient presented with central chest pain starting at about 11:00 while gardening.
The patient experienced heavy central chest pain radiating to the left arm, lasting about 30 minutes, and is currently experiencing pain at a severity of 3/10.
The patient has associated sweating and mild breathlessness, but no nausea.
The patient has no previous similar episodes or known cardiac disease.
The patient has a history of hypertension.
The patient is a smoker, consuming about 20 cigarettes per day.
The patient's father had a myocardial infarction at age 52.
The patient received 300 mg of aspirin and a GTN spray from the ambulance crew.
The patient is taking amlodipine 5 mg once daily.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient's heart rate is 88 and regular.
The patient's blood pressure is 152/90.
The patient's oxygen level is 97% on air.
The patient's heart sounds are normal.
The patient's chest is clear.
There is no peripheral oedema.
The ECG shows sinus rhythm with 1 mm ST depression in leads V4 to V6.
The impression is suspected acute coronary syndrome (possible NSTEMI).
The plan includes serial high-sensitivity troponin testing, fondaparinux 2.5 mg subcutaneously once daily, and GTN spray as required.
The patient is to be admitted under the cardiology team for a likely coronary angiography.
The patient was instructed to report recurrent or worsening pain to nursing staff immediately.

transcript_facts.fact: Patient reported getting pain in chest while digging in the garden.
Patient reported the pain started about eleven o'clock, after lunch, or just before eleven, after putting the kettle on.
Patient described the pain location as the middle of the chest, like a heavy weight.
Patient reported the pain went down their left arm.
The pain lasted about half an hour and is currently at a severity of three out of ten.
Patient reported feeling very sweaty but not sick.
Patient reported feeling a bit short of breath.
Patient stated they have never had this before.
Patient stated they have no heart problems in the past but is on amlodipine.
Patient's amlodipine dose is five milligrams.
Patient stated they smoke about twenty cigarettes a day.
Patient's father had a heart attack at age 52.
Relative stated their father had a heart attack at age 60.
Paramedics gave the patient aspirin 300 milligrams and a GTN spray.
Examination findings: Heart rate is 88 and regular, blood pressure is 152 over 90, heart sounds are normal, chest is clear, and oxygen level is 97 percent.
ECG shows about a millimetre of ST depression in the leads on the left side of the chest, V4 to V6.
Clinician stated it is possible the condition is an acute coronary syndrome and a blood test for troponin was taken.
Clinician stated the plan is to start an injection called fondaparinux, 2.5 milligrams under the skin once a day, and to have a GTN spray if pain returns.
Clinician stated the plan is to admit the patient under the cardiology team for a likely coronary angiography.
Clinician stated they will repeat the ECG every time the patient gets pain and instructed the patient to tell nurses immediately if pain returns or gets worse.
